description: Tracks oracle (Gemini) factual accuracy. Hallucinations are cases where the oracle confidently stated something factually wrong, not just miscalibrated.

hallucinations.question: Will foreign airlines resume commercial passenger flights to Tel Aviv (TLV) by March 15, 2026?
hallucinations.oracle_claim: Airlines have already resumed flights, security situation stabilized
hallucinations.reality: First scheduled resumptions: American Airlines March 28, Emirates March 31

hallucinations.question: One Battle After Another wins Best Picture?
hallucinations.oracle_claim: No film titled 'One Battle After Another' exists among 2026 nominees; title appears fictional
hallucinations.reality: Paul Thomas Anderson film with 13 Oscar nominations, frontrunner (won BAFTAs, DGA, PGA, Critics Choice, Golden Globe)

hallucinations.question: Will either a state or the US government name something after Charlie Kirk by EOY 2026?
hallucinations.oracle_claim: No legislative momentum or public proposal suggesting naming honor; Kirk is a living activist
hallucinations.reality: Kirk was assassinated Sep 2025. Arizona Senate passed SB1010 renaming Loop 202 after Kirk on Feb 18, 2026. SC also pursuing road naming

hallucinations.question: One Battle After Another wins Best Picture? (repeat)
hallucinations.oracle_claim: 0% probability for frontrunner winning Best Picture
hallucinations.reality: Film swept all precursors (BAFTA, Critics Choice, Golden Globe, DGA, PGA). Oscars ceremony same day. 79% market probability reasonable

hallucinations.question: Significant advancement in frontier AI model architecture by EOY 2026
hallucinations.oracle_claim: 75% YES based on 'improved reasoning chains' and 'test-time compute scaling'
hallucinations.reality: Market asks about non-transformer ARCHITECTURE (MoE doesn't count), not capability improvements. Oracle answered a completely different question. Market at 21% is well-calibrated for the actual criteria

hallucinations.question: WTI Crude Oil above $95 on March 20
hallucinations.oracle_claim: WTI crude oil is currently trading significantly below $95
hallucinations.reality: WTI at $98.10 and rising due to Iran war escalation

summary.pattern: Oracle most dangerous when: (1) claiming verifiable things don't exist with high confidence, (2) using stale world models that miss major events (assassinations, legislative actions), (3) extreme overconfidence on near-term factual claims, (4) answering a different question than the market is actually asking (comprehension failure — the oracle reads the title but misses resolution criteria that narrowly scope the question). The bigger the oracle's confidence on a verifiable claim, the more verification is needed.
